turns.prompt:
You are given an attached CSV file b3_fatigue_data.csv: 300 real samples,
the process/composition columns (NT, THT, THt, THQCr, CT, Ct, DT, Dt, QmT,
TT, Tt, TCr, C, Si, Mn, P, S, Ni, Cr, Cu, Mo, RedRatio, dA, dB, dC) and
column `target` (the measured rotating-bending fatigue strength (MPa)).

Propose a recipe (a value for each variable below), within each observed
range, that MAXIMIZES rotating-bending fatigue strength (MPa) AND stays
robust — its rotating-bending fatigue strength (MPa) must not collapse under
a ±5% change in any single variable (seek a broad optimum, not a sharp
peak). Design variables:
  - NT (value in [825, 930])
  - THT (value in [30, 865])
  - THt (value in [0, 30])
  - THQCr (value in [0, 24])
  - CT (value in [30, 930])
  - Ct (value in [0, 540])
  - DT (value in [30, 903.333])
  - Dt (value in [0, 70.2])
  - QmT (value in [30, 140])
  - TT (value in [30, 680])
  - Tt (value in [0, 120])
  - TCr (value in [0, 24])
  - C (value in [0.17, 0.63])
  - Si (value in [0.16, 2.05])
  - Mn (value in [0.37, 1.6])
  - P (value in [0.002, 0.031])
  - S (value in [0.003, 0.03])
  - Ni (value in [0.01, 2.78])
  - Cr (value in [0.01, 1.17])
  - Cu (value in [0.01, 0.26])
  - Mo (value in [0, 0.24])
  - RedRatio (value in [240, 5530])
  - dA (value in [0, 0.13])
  - dB (value in [0, 0.05])
  - dC (value in [0, 0.058])

Reason from the training data, then end with your explicit proposal, e.g.
"Final: NT=877.5, THT=447.5, THt=15, THQCr=12, CT=480, Ct=270, DT=466.666,
Dt=35.1, QmT=85, TT=355, Tt=60, TCr=12, C=0.4, Si=1.105, Mn=0.985, P=0.0165,
S=0.0165, Ni=1.395, Cr=0.59, Cu=0.135, Mo=0.12, RedRatio=2885, dA=0.065,
dB=0.025, dC=0.029".
turns.answer_text:
## Analysis

**Identifying the high-strength regime.** Sorting by `target`, every sample above ~1000 MPa shares a very consistent processing signature that is clearly distinct from the mid/low performers:

| Variable | Top cluster (target > 1000) |
|---|---|
| NT | 930 (max) |
| THT / THt / THQCr | 30 / 0 / 0 (no through-hardening step) |
| CT | 930 (max) |
| DT | ~850–896 (high) |
| Dt | 15–70 |
| QmT | 60–140 |
| TT | 160–200 (low-temperature temper) |
| Tt | 120 (max) |
| TCr | 0.5 |
| C | 0.17–0.23 (low) |
| Cr | 0.45–1.17 (high) |
| Ni | 0.02–1.69 |
| Mo | 0.15–0.21 |
| RedRatio | 240–860 |

The pattern is a **high-austenitizing + full carburize/quench + low-temperature temper** route on a **low-C, high-hardenability (Cr/Ni/Mo) alloy**. This regime dominates the top of the dataset (1000–1190 MPa), while the low group (through-hardened, THT≈845, high TT≈550–650) tops out much lower.

**Robustness.** Because there are many samples in this cluster reaching 1050–1190 MPa across a range of Ct, Dt, QmT, Ni and Cr, the optimum is *broad*, not a spike. Two sub-families both work: (Ni≈1.6, Cr≈0.55) and (Ni≈0.06, Cr≈1.17). I therefore choose **central, interior values** of the cluster (Ni≈1.0, Cr≈0.8, mid-range Ct/Dt/QmT) so that a ±5% perturbation of any single variable stays comfortably inside the observed high-strength region — never falling onto a boundary or into the low-strength (high-TT/through-hardened) regime.

- NT=930 stays saturated at max; ±5% still ≥883 (still top-cluster).
- TT kept low (~180); ±5% keeps it well below the 550+ low-strength zone.
- C kept ~0.21 (interior of 0.17–0.23), Cr/Ni/Mo moderate-high for hardenability margin.
- RedRatio=690 sits in the middle of the winning band.

## Proposal

**Final: NT=930, THT=30, THt=0, THQCr=0, CT=930, Ct=450, DT=890, Dt=50, QmT=100, TT=180, Tt=120, TCr=0.5, C=0.21, Si=0.30, Mn=0.70, P=0.013, S=0.015, Ni=1.0, Cr=0.80, Cu=0.10, Mo=0.15, RedRatio=690, dA=0.05, dB=0.005, dC=0.005**
